title: Did Sex Jump-Start Evolution?
hook: Earth's first animals barely changed for ages. A study argues the switch from cloning to sex is what finally set evolution — and biodiversity — racing.
key_points: Earth's earliest animals reproduced largely asexually and changed little over long spans.
Asexual cloning makes near-identical offspring, limiting the variation evolution needs.
Sexual reproduction shuffles two parents' genes into new combinations each generation.
The study links the shift toward sex to a surge in biodiversity and faster evolution.
content_html: For hundreds of millions of years, Earth's earliest animals barely changed. A new study suggests the reason lies in how they reproduced — and that the switch to sex is what finally set evolution racing.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, the research argues that early animal communities reproduced largely asexually, cloning themselves into genetically similar, low-competition populations that stayed evolutionarily stagnant. Sexual reproduction changes that: it shuffles two parents' genes into novel combinations every generation, generating the raw genetic variety that natural selection feeds on. As environmental pressures pushed animals toward sex, that variation — and the competition it fueled — accelerated diversification, helping set the stage for the explosion of animal forms that followed. The work reframes sex not just as a way to make offspring, but as an engine of evolutionary change.

related.title: Sexual Selection
related.hook: Why does a peacock drag around a tail that makes it easy prey? Because for some traits, winning a mate matters more to evolution than simply surviving.

related.title: How New Species Form
related.hook: Split one population in two, let them drift apart long enough, and eventually they can no longer interbreed — that's speciation, the engine that fills the tree of life with branches.

related.title: The Cambrian Explosion
related.hook: Around 540 million years ago, after billions of years of mostly microbes, animal life suddenly diversified into a riot of body plans — most major groups appearing in a geological blink.

flashcards.prompt: Why does sexual reproduction tend to speed up evolution?
flashcards.back_html: It shuffles two parents' genes into new combinations every generation, creating the genetic variety that natural selection acts on.

flashcards.prompt: Per the study, why did Earth's earliest animals change so little for so long?

choices.text: They reproduced asexually, forming genetically similar, low-competition communities
They had no genes for natural selection to act on
The planet was frozen solid the entire time

flashcards.explanation_html: Cloning produced near-identical offspring with little competition, so these early communities stayed evolutionarily stagnant.

flashcards.prompt: What does the research say the shift toward sexual reproduction triggered?

choices.text: A surge in biodiversity and faster evolution
The extinction of all animal life

flashcards.explanation_html: Once environmental pressures pushed animals toward sex, the new genetic variety and competition it created accelerated diversification.
